title: Comparative study of chemical treatments on the mechanical and moisture absorption behavior of coccinia indica fiber-reinforced epoxy composites
desc: Rising demand for eco-conscious-based functional material drives the focus of materials science field scientists towards research on natural fiber-reinforced polymer composites (NFRPCs), which hold significant attention due to their high strength-to-weight ratio and sustainability. For further enhancement, composites are reinforced with surface-treated fibers, which exhibit optimal performance. This work focuses on fabricating epoxy composites reinforced with Coccinia indica fiber. Different surface-treating chemicals were utilised to determine the optimal chemical and its concentration to obtain effective mechanical and water absorption properties of the composite. Results revealed that Coccinia indica fiber-reinforced epoxy composite reinforced with 0.5% of KMnO4 showed superior performance with a tensile strength of 40.13 MPa and a flexural strength of 89.74 MPa. The compression strength and impact strength of this composite were recorded as 50 MPa and 650 J/m, respectively. By comparison, the untreated CIF/epoxy composite exhibited a tensile strength of 34.59 MPa, flexural strength of 66.63 MPa, compressive strength of 34.4 MPa, and impact strength of 386.7 J/m. The failure mechanism of the fractured samples was determined by employing SEM analysis. Hydrophilic characteristics were determined through the water absorption process, revealing the lowest water intake percentage for this composite, indicating the effective function of KMnO4 in bonding between the matrix and reinforcement. These findings suggest Coccinia indica fiber-reinforced epoxy composite reinforced with 0.5% of KMnO4 as a viable alternative to conventional materials, offering a balanced combination of performance, cost-effectiveness, and environmental advantage for semi-structural and automobile applications.

title: Breastfeeding self-efficacy in mothers and its association with maternal functioning, maternal knowledge, and attitudes toward breastfeeding: a cross-sectional study
desc: Breastfeeding constitutes a cornerstone intervention, delivering extensive benefits to children, women, and society. Although breastfeeding self-efficacy plays a crucial role in the initiation and continuation of breastfeeding, evidence regarding the factors associated with breastfeeding self-efficacy remains limited in Iran. This study aimed to examine breastfeeding Self-Efficacy in Mothers and Its Association with Maternal Functioning, Maternal Knowledge, and Attitudes Toward Breastfeeding. This cross-sectional study involved 245 breastfeeding mothers with infants under 6 months of age, recruited via multistage cluster sampling. Participants completed five assessment tools for evaluating demographic and obstetric characteristics, infant feeding attitudes, breastfeeding knowledge, maternal functioning, and breastfeeding self-efficacy (BES). Univariate and multiple linear regression analyses were conducted to identify predictors of breastfeeding self-efficacy. The mean (SD) scores of maternal functioning, breastfeeding self-efficacy, breastfeeding knowledge, and feeding attitude were 113.71 (13.83), 56.29 (7.38), 5.42 (1.45), and 52.91 (6.40), respectively. Pearson’s correlation analysis showed positive associations between breastfeeding self-efficacy and knowledge (r = 0.552, P < 0.001), feeding attitude (r = 0.413, P < 0.001), and maternal functioning (r = 0.308, P < 0.001). In the final adjusted regression model, which included previous breastfeeding experience, the model explained 32.4% of the variance in breastfeeding self-efficacy. Breastfeeding knowledge remained a significant independent predictor (β = 0.441, P < 0.001), as did previous breastfeeding experience (B = 1.628, P = 0.039), whereas feeding attitude and maternal functioning were not statistically significant after adjustment. Breastfeeding knowledge was the strongest independent predictor of breastfeeding self-efficacy, and previous breastfeeding experience was also independently associated with higher self-efficacy after adjustment. Although feeding attitude and maternal functioning were positively associated with breastfeeding self-efficacy in unadjusted analyses, their associations were not statistically significant in the final adjusted model. These findings highlight the potential importance of strengthening breastfeeding knowledge and building on mothers’ previous breastfeeding experiences in interventions aimed at improving breastfeeding self-efficacy.

title: Differentiated service delivery and peer-led digital messages to strengthen health outcomes among young men and non-binary persons who have sex with men in Brazil
desc: Despite the disproportionate burden of HIV among young men and non-binary persons who have sex with men (YMSM/NB) in Latin America, interventions among this population are scarce. We aimed to evaluate changes in health outcomes associated with a targeted intervention. Conectad@s was a 48-week single-arm study among Brazilian YMSM/NB (18–24 years) using an intervention combining differentiated service delivery (DSD) and peer-led weekly digital messages. We used generalized estimating equations to evaluate changes over time during two periods: (1) DSD plus weekly messages (weeks 0–24) and (2) DSD only (weeks 24–48). All 409 YMSM/NB accepted the intervention; 83.4% were retained to 48 weeks. During the first period, we observed increased odds of current ART use (aOR:1.14[99.7%CI 1.05–1.23]), current oral PrEP use (aOR:1.17[99.7%CI 1.14–1.20]), and good self-rated health (aOR:1.03[99.7%CI 1.02–1.05), and decreased odds of binge drinking (aOR:0.97[99.7%CI 0.95–0.99]), depressive symptoms (aOR:0.97[99.7%CI 0.95–0.98]), and anxiety (aOR:0.97[99.7%CI 0.96–0.99]). During the second period, we observed decreases on moderate/high problematic substance use (aOR:0.96[99.7%CI 0.95–0.98]). Most participants reported they would recommend text messages for supporting HIV prevention and treatment (99.4%) and found the weekly frequency to be adequate (92.1%). Our findings support the potential of integrated, LGBTQIAPN + -affirming DSD with digitally tailored engagement strategies to address persistent gaps in HIV prevention and care among YMSM/NB.
